title: Pinch Your Nose and Try to Hum #science #body
description:
Close your lips, pinch your nose, and hum. The hum stops after a moment. When you hum, the air leaves through your nose. Pinch it shut, and the air piles up in your mouth and throat, above your vocal folds. The pressure there climbs until it almost matches the pressure in your lungs. With almost no pressure difference across them, the vocal folds stop vibrating, and the sound stops. Let go, and the hum comes back.

More: Episode 7 (why your fingers wrinkle in water) [link added at upload]

Sources

- Titze, I. R., Phonation threshold pressure (vocology.utah.edu)
- Dummies, Improving Your Singing: Moving Air Through the Nose (dummies.com)
- The head cutaway and pressure bars are a sketch, not to scale; the fading hum is shown in slow motion

Try it: how long does your hum last?

Script, voice and animation are AI-produced (Claude; Kokoro voice). Every claim is checked against the sources above.

subtitles: Close your lips, pinch your nose, and hum.
Keep humming, as long as you can.
Air fills your mouth, and the hum is gone.
When you hum, the air leaves through your nose.
Pinch your nose shut, and the air piles up above your vocal folds.
The pressure there climbs until it almost matches your lungs.
With no push across them, the folds stop vibrating.
Pinch your nose, and try again.
